common:
Date: <<DATE>>. You are one worker in a saturation sweep of the public repository seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack: a portable reference stack of native agent tooling (Claude Code, Codex, MCP, memory/RAG, token efficiency, CI/supply chain, observability) whose north star is US-equities research and historical simulation (NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 with an IBKR destination and a separate Alpaca adapter; LEAN as comparison engine), followed by independently qualified paper trading. Live trading is out of scope.
Hosts: linux-wsl2-x86_64 GPU workstation (Threadripper PRO 5975WX 48 CPUs, 102 GiB RAM, RTX 4090 24 GB, Ada: FP8 native, NVFP4 not native) and macos-arm64 Macs (M5 Pro, 24 GB and 64 GB).
Selection principles: native accounts and supported upstream installation; maintained upstream, by a rule derived from the OpenSSF Scorecard Maintained check (https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#maintained), which scores an archived repository lowest, uses a 90-day window and gives its top score to at least one commit per week and partial credit for maintainers' issue activity: a repository is stale, and excluded whatever its stars, when it is archived or has no commit on its default branch in the last 90 days (establish this with gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits?since=<date 90 days ago>&per_page=1 or the same https://api.github.com REST URL, not from pushed_at, which counts any branch; a lane that cannot reach either source, such as a web-only lane, records the commit fact as unknown and never excludes or refutes a repository on unknown maintenance, because a missing result is pending, never refuted); this rule excludes only the zero-activity end, so record lower activity as a maintenance fact without excluding; a repository created less than 90 days ago is too new to assess and must say so at the start of its demonstrated_gap ("TOO NEW TO ASSESS (<90 days): ..."); an old release tag on an actively committed branch is not stale (pin the commit when a needed fix exists only on the branch); licenses are recorded as information only and are never a reason to exclude, refute or rank down a candidate (the operator's private experimental environment); no paid SaaS or new credentials unless a demonstrated gap requires it; local-first and privacy-filtered; evidence over popularity (stars and install counts are never evidence of fit).
Rules: primary sources only (GitHub API/pages for releases, tags, stars, pushed_at, archived, license, renames; official docs and changelogs; Hugging Face model cards). Cite the URL for every fact. Read-only: never install, clone-and-run, or execute candidate code; never read or print credentials. Canonical repository form: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> (follow renames to the current owner). Answer only in the required JSON.
Skills (installed from adoption/skills/manifest.json, the pinned <<SKILLS_CHECKED_AT>> skills trial): use the ones that fit your role and record every skill you actually used in skills_used. Discovery: search-first (survey maintained upstream options before judging) and iterative-retrieval (staged, bounded retrieval). Refutation (evidence before any verdict): supply-chain-risk-auditor (maintenance, ownership, advisories, archived/renamed upstreams) and fp-check (verify a claim before calling it true or false). Layer-specific where relevant: agentic-actions-auditor (CI and GitHub automation), security-threat-model / codeql / semgrep / sarif-parsing (security and supply chain), property-based-testing (quality evaluation), mcp-builder (MCP surfaces), modern-python (Python tooling), agent-browser (JavaScript-heavy pages you cannot read otherwise). In Claude Code invoke a skill with the Skill tool; in Codex mention it as $skill-name. Do not load skills you do not use.
Merit, not incumbency: the current winners are provisional. Being the current winner, the retained control (for example ai-memory in durable-memory is recorded as the retained control, not a measured best), popular, or already installed is NOT evidence of quality. Judge every repository, winners included, on current evidence: measured quality on this requirement (benchmarks, retained comparisons), SOTA-ness (recent releases, capability), maintenance and supply-chain health, and platform fit (license is information only). A candidate that is plausibly better than a winner on such evidence has a demonstrated gap. Report in notes any winner whose standing rests on incumbency rather than evidence.
discover:
ROLE: discovery researcher for ONE layer.
Layer input (requirement, current winners and pins, alternatives, upstream drift, open gaps, the previous sweep's survivors/refuted, repositories already known, and seeded candidates from other sessions):
<<LAYER_INPUT>>
<<STARS_NOTE>>
Task: find the strongest CURRENT candidates that could beat, replace or usefully complement this layer's winners for THIS requirement on these hosts. Cover: newest releases and models (last 4 weeks especially), strongly maintained community projects, the seeded candidates (assess every seeded item that is a repository: propose it with the right label or say in notes why not), and any winner health change (archived, renamed, relicensed, major release) which you report in notes.
Propose at most 6 repositories. Label each:
- targeted_candidate: worth a bounded native trial against the winner now (a concrete gap and a feasible trial on these hosts).
- keep_but_compare: credible alternative to compare when the requirement or evidence changes.
- not_adopted: checked and not worth pursuing (give the decisive reason) -- use this for a prominent/seeded repository you rejected so the rejection is recorded.
For each: repository; proposed_label; demonstrated_gap (the specific requirement gap versus the current winners, concrete, not generic praise); comparison_that_would_overturn (the measurable comparison that would decide it); evidence (URLs, each with what it shows); upstream_now (latest_release tag, released_at date, stars, pushed_at, archived, license -- from the GitHub API or page; null when unknowable); source (how you found it).
Record your call counts in calls (web_search, web_fetch, gh_api). Put winner-health observations and any seeded item you did not propose in notes. Set layer_id to <<LAYER_ID>>.
Research budget (hard): at most 12 web searches, 8 page fetches and 40 GitHub API calls for this layer; stop researching when the budget is spent and answer with what you verified.
discover_skills:
ROLE: skills discovery researcher for ONE lifecycle task. In this modality the unit is a skill (one SKILL.md folder in a source repository), not a repository.
Layer input (the lifecycle task and its requirement, the installed skills with their pins and invocation flags, the task's skill sources with pinned commits, open gaps, the previous sweep's survivors/refuted, the manifest's installed and excluded skills (known_skills), and seeded candidates from other sessions):
<<LAYER_INPUT>>
<<STARS_NOTE>>
Task: find the strongest CURRENT skills that could beat, replace or usefully complement the installed skills for THIS task on these hosts, in Claude Code and in Codex. Search the task's sources first (their SKILL.md folders on the default branch, read through the GitHub API), then beyond them: official vendor skill repositories, curated lists, and the skills.sh registry through the skills manifest's pinned CLI (DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx skills@1.7.0 find <query>) where you can run commands, or its listing pages where you cannot. Cover skills published or substantially revised in the last 4 weeks, the seeded candidates (assess every seeded skill: propose it with the right label or say in notes why not), and any installed skill's health change (moved, removed, renamed, relicensed, or its invocation flags changed upstream), which you report in notes.
The selection principles above apply to each skill's source repository: its maintenance rule excludes a stale source (archived, or no default-branch commit in the last 90 days, established from evidence; unknown maintenance never excludes or refutes). A source whose layer-input entry carries a maintenance record with status stale failed that rule when the skills catalog was checked (its evidence field holds the API fact): label its skills not_adopted and cite the record, unless you find a maintained fork or replacement, which you propose in their place (its installed skills are replacement targets, named in the task's open gaps). Evidence over popularity: skills.sh install counts, registry rank, audit badges and GitHub stars are discovery guides, never evidence of quality or fit. Primary sources only: the SKILL.md at the pinned commit, the agents/openai.yaml beside it, and the source repository's GitHub API. Read-only: never install a skill (no npx skills add, no $skill-installer), clone-and-run, or execute a skill's scripts. A skill that makes intake, brainstorming or a planning approval mandatory for bounded work, writes into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md on its own initiative, or tells the model to install unpinned code conflicts with this repository's canonical instructions: label it not_adopted with that reason. Editing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md when asked is not such a write: it is the skills-agent-docs task's requirement.
Propose at most 6 skills. Label each:
- targeted_candidate: worth a bounded paired trial against the installed skill for this task now (a concrete gap and a feasible trial on these hosts).
- keep_but_compare: credible alternative to compare when the requirement or evidence changes.
- not_adopted: checked and not worth pursuing (give the decisive reason) -- use this for a prominent or seeded skill you rejected so the rejection is recorded.
For each: skill_ref (owner/repo@name, where name is the SKILL.md name field, which the Agent Skills specification requires to match its folder name); source_id (the layer input's source_id that holds the skill, or "unlisted"); lifecycle_task (the layer input's lifecycle_task); pin (the 40-hex commit of the source's default branch at which you read the SKILL.md); skill_md_sha256 (sha256 of the SKILL.md bytes at that pin, computed with a command, or null when you cannot run commands); license (the SKILL.md license field or the repository's SPDX id; null when unknown; information only); source (how you found it); description_chars (Unicode code points of the frontmatter description, surrounding whitespace stripped, as the skills manifest counts them); model_invocable (false when the SKILL.md frontmatter sets a true-valued disable-model-invocation (true/yes/on/1) in any letter case, or its agents/openai.yaml sets policy allow_implicit_invocation to a plain false, else true); codex_implicit (false when that agents/openai.yaml sets policy allow_implicit_invocation to a plain false, else true: Codex reads the file with serde_yaml and ignores it when the value is quoted or another word such as no); replaces (the installed skill of this task it would replace, or null for a complement); proposed_label; demonstrated_gap (the specific gap versus the installed skills for THIS task, concrete, not generic praise); evidence (URLs, each with what it shows); upstream_now (the source repository's latest_release tag, released_at date, stars, pushed_at, archived, license -- from the GitHub API or page; null when unknowable); comparison_that_would_overturn (the measurable comparison that would decide it: skill-creator's paired with-skill/without-skill benchmark or a promptfoo config on a frozen set of this task's prompts, naming the arms, the metric and the decision rule).
Record your call counts in calls (web_search, web_fetch, gh_api; a registry query counts as a web_search). Put installed-skill health observations and any seeded item you did not propose in notes. Set layer_id to <<LAYER_ID>>.
Research budget (hard): at most 12 web searches, 8 page fetches and 40 GitHub API calls for this layer; stop researching when the budget is spent and answer with what you verified.
facts:
ROLE: facts/identity refuter for ONE layer. Assume every proposal below may contain a false or unsupported fact.
Layer: <<LAYER_ID>> -- requirement: <<REQUIREMENT>>
Proposals (JSON):
<<PROPOSALS>>
For EACH proposal check with primary sources (GitHub API/pages via gh api or fetch; official docs): the repository exists at that canonical URL (or its rename), is not archived or abandoned contrary to the claim, and the license, latest release, release date, stars/activity and every cited evidence URL actually say what the proposal claims. Vote refuted=true if any material factual claim is false, unsupported by its cited source, or unverifiable; refuted=false only when you verified the facts. Default to refuted=true when uncertain. Unknown fields, maintenance and license are the exceptions (the selection principles): a null upstream_now field means unknown, not a false claim; record an unverifiable commit or activity fact as unknown, and a wrong or unverifiable license as a correction or as unknown, in your reasoning; none of these is a reason to refute. Give confidence 0..1, short reasoning, and the refs (URLs) you checked. One vote per proposal, same repository string. Set role to facts and layer_id to <<LAYER_ID>>.
Verification budget (hard): at most 8 web searches, 10 page fetches and 30 GitHub API calls in total for all proposals.<<MODALITY>>
fit:
ROLE: fit/standing refuter for ONE layer. Assume every proposal below is wrong for this repository and try to break it.
Layer input:
<<LAYER_INPUT>>
Proposals (JSON):
<<PROPOSALS>>
For EACH proposal vote refuted=true if ANY holds: no concrete, evidence-backed gap versus the current winners for THIS requirement (a plausible advantage in measured quality, SOTA-ness, maintenance or fit counts; incumbency does not count for the winner); it duplicates a winner or an already-known alternative without new evidence; it does not support linux x86_64/WSL2 or macOS arm64 where the layer needs it; it is infeasible on the hosts (e.g. needs more than 24 GB VRAM or more RAM than available, or NVFP4-only weights on Ada); it is stale under the selection principles' maintenance rule (archived, or no default-branch commit in the last 90 days, established from evidence; unknown maintenance is never a reason to refute); it requires a paid SaaS or new credentials without a gap that justifies it; it conflicts with the selection principles; or its label is wrong (a targeted_candidate with no feasible bounded trial, or a not_adopted whose rejection reason is itself wrong). Vote refuted=false only when the proposal and its label hold up. Default to refuted=true when uncertain. Give confidence 0..1, reasoning, refs. One vote per proposal, same repository string. Set role to fit and layer_id to <<LAYER_ID>>.
Verification budget (hard): at most 8 web searches, 10 page fetches and 30 GitHub API calls in total for all proposals.<<MODALITY>>
modality_skills: SKILLS MODALITY: each proposal above is a skill; its repository field holds its skill_ref (owner/repo@name), so vote with that exact string as repository, and read the proposal's skill fields (source_id, lifecycle_task, pin, skill_md_sha256, license, description_chars, model_invocable, codex_implicit, replaces). Facts refuter: check that the SKILL.md exists in that repository at pin with that name field (git trees or contents API at the commit); that skill_md_sha256, when not null, is the sha256 of its bytes at pin; that description_chars counts the frontmatter description's Unicode code points, surrounding whitespace stripped; that model_invocable is false exactly when the frontmatter sets a true-valued disable-model-invocation (true/yes/on/1) in any letter case or the agents/openai.yaml beside it sets policy allow_implicit_invocation to a plain false; that codex_implicit is false exactly when that openai.yaml does (Codex ignores the file when the value is quoted or another word such as no); and that replaces names an installed skill of this layer or is null. A wrong invocation flag or sha256 is a material false claim. Fit refuter: refute also when comparison_that_would_overturn names neither skill-creator's paired with-skill/without-skill benchmark nor a promptfoo config with a frozen task set and a decision rule; when the layer's requirement needs a model-invocable skill and model_invocable is false; when the skill duplicates an installed skill or a skill the layer input's known_skills lists as installed or excluded, without new evidence; or when it conflicts with the canonical instructions (it makes intake, brainstorming or a planning approval mandatory for bounded work, writes into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md on its own initiative, or tells the model to install unpinned code; editing those files when asked is the skills-agent-docs task's requirement, not a conflict). A source whose layer-input entry has maintenance status stale is stale under the selection principles' maintenance rule; its evidence field holds the API fact. Install counts, registry rank and stars never count as evidence of fit.
critic:
ROLE: completeness critic for a <<LAYER_COUNT>>-layer saturation sweep. Below is a compact summary of every layer: requirement, winners, what was proposed and what survived both refuters.
<<SUMMARY>>
Find at most 8 layers where discovery most likely MISSED a strong current candidate class (a newest release or model from the last 4 weeks, a whole category of tools, a platform-specific option for linux-wsl2 RTX 4090 or macOS arm64, a north-star research or simulation runtime, a security or supply-chain option). For each give the layer_id, the reason, and 2-5 concrete search directions. Also list general observations (e.g. systematic bias). Do not re-propose candidates already proposed.
critic_skills:
ROLE: completeness critic for a <<LAYER_COUNT>>-layer skills sweep. Each layer is one lifecycle task and each proposal one skill (owner/repo@name). Below is a compact summary of every layer: what was proposed and what survived the refuters.
<<SUMMARY>>
Find at most 8 layers where discovery most likely MISSED a strong current skill class: a skill published or substantially revised in the last 4 weeks, a source the layer's sources do not cover (an official vendor repository, a curated list, a registry listing), a Codex skill with agents/openai.yaml or a Claude Code-only one, a model-invocable alternative where the installed skill is user-invoked only (design-intake and architecture require model invocation), or an evaluation skill for the skill lifecycle (skill-creator's paired benchmark, promptfoo). For each give the layer_id, the reason, and 2-5 concrete search directions (a repository, a query for npx skills@1.7.0 find, or a skill name). Also list general observations (e.g. systematic bias toward popular registries or one vendor). Install counts, registry rank and stars are discovery guides, never evidence. Do not re-propose skills already proposed.
